newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer, trade quiet ahead of FOMC, auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer, trade quiet ahead of FOMC, auction.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended slightly firmer on Tuesday on light position adjustment ahead of a Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later in the day and a 10-year JGB auction planned on Wednesday.
"Traders are mostly taking a wait-and-see stance ahead of the FOMC and 10-year JGB auction," said a city bank trader.

The market was divided in two, with those who expect the FOMC to raise the Federal Fund (FF) rate by 25 basis points on one side, and those who expect the FOMC to keep interest rates unchanged on the other, traders said.
The December contract ended at 122.11, up just slightly from Friday's 122.10, after moving in a range of 121.95 to 122.17 during the day.
Monday was a national holiday and markets were closed.
Regardless of whether the FOMC decides to raise interest rates or not, traders said they expected little lasting effect on the JGB market.
"If a rise of 25 basis points takes place, JGBs may be sold somewhat temporarily, but otherwise there will be no effect," said a trust bank trader.
The coupon rate for 10-year government bonds to be offered through an auction on Wednesday will probably be 2.9 percent, possibly 2.8 percent, traders said.
There probably will not be much demand for these JGBs even if the coupon rate is set at 2.9 percent, traders said.
"Since interest rates are unlikely to dip from current levels, it would be difficult to buy at the auction if the coupon rate turns out to be 2.9 percent," the trust bank trader said.
A coupon rate of 2.8 percent would deter investors and cause many to opt out of the auction, dealers said.
A coupon rate of 2.9 percent would be equal to the lowest ever for 10-year JGBs offered through an auction, a rate last seen in last October's 10-year JGB auction.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGB was yielding 2.840 percent as of 0701 GMT, down from Friday's 2.845 percent.
Traders said hedge sales caused the December contract to fall in the morning.
The December contract recovered its losses in late afternoon trade on position adjustment, they said. -- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-5473-3748)
